content.text: Dear Anthony,

Thanks for your interest in our Nationals beat writer opening. Once we have reviewed materials submitted by all the candidates, we will be in touch if we need any further information or want to discuss the position further. We receive many applications for all our openings so I thank you in advance for your patience as we review clips.
Sincerely,
Matt Vita
Matthew Vita
Sports Editor | The Washington Post

From: Anthony Fenech [mailto:anthonyfenech@hotmail.com] 
Sent: Monday, December 17, 2018 1:05 PM
To: Vita, Matthew <Matthew.Vita@washpost.com>; Rennie, Matthew <Matthew.Rennie@washpost.com>; Yoder, Glenn <Glenn.Yoder@washpost.com>; Grant, Tracy <Tracy.Grant@washpost.com>
Subject: Nationals beat writer candidate - Anthony Fenech
[EXTERNAL EMAIL]
Hello Matt, Matt, Glenn and Tracy,
My name is Anthony Fenech and I cover the Tigers for the Detroit Free Press. I'm e-mailing to apply for the Nationals beat writer job opening.

In my four years on the Tigers beat, I've built a unique brand of coverage that stands out in one of the country's best baseball cities. I've done this by building relationships throughout the game, outworking the competition and creatively telling stories on multiple platforms with a consistent social media voice. I break news competitively and I am a good teammate. My reporting style is a blend of old-school ideals and new-school skills, and my passion for the process shows in my work. Last year, I placed in the Top 10 in the Associated Press Sports Editors top beat writing category.

I'm applying for this job because I'm ready for a new challenge in my career, one which furthers my development as a reporter and writer. I consider myself an ideal fit for your beat and I'm confident in my belief that if you hear more about the way I cover a beat, you will, too.
Attached is my resume, and I have included links to my work below. If you need anything else, please let me know. Thank you for your time.
Anthony
